A Recomputed Block Beside a Filter in the Jeffreys Derivatives

Source: R/jfp_move.R
jfp_movers.Rd

Returns the parts of the derivatives of the predictors that come from a term whose block is recomputed at the coefficients (modelterms7::nl(), a smoothed modelterms7::seg()) in a model with a filter: jfp_static_rows() the part of \(\partial^{1+|S|}\eta/\partial u\,\partial S\) for one or two directions, one matrix per equation over every coordinate, and jfp_static_curv() the part of \(\sum_t\sum_c g_{c,t}\, \partial^{2+|S|}\eta_{c,t}/\partial u^2\partial S\) for none, one or two directions. jfp_movers() returns the terms, and jfp_static_aug() the predictors' derivatives with further unknowns whose static rows are given.

Usage

jfp_movers(st)

jfp_static_aug(st, cols)

jfp_static_block(st, name, f)

jfp_static_pairs(st, name, f)

jfp_static_xvw(st, v, w)

jfp_static_rows(st, dirs)

jfp_static_curv(st, g, dirs = list())

Arguments

st

A state, from jfp_state(), of a model with a filter.

cols

A list of column blocks, each a list with name and rows (one matrix or NULL per distribution parameter).

name

The name of a block of columns.

f

A function of a unit returning the block's static rows in the unit's equation.

v, w

Directions over every coordinate.

dirs

A list of directions over every coordinate (the full width of the filter's rows).

g

A named list of per-observation weights, already multiplied by the observation weights.

Value

jfp_static_rows() one matrix per distribution parameter over every coordinate; jfp_static_curv() a square matrix over every coordinate; jfp_movers() the units of refresh_units(); jfp_static_aug() what jfp_joint_rows() returns, with pos (the columns of each block), oi (the columns of the original coordinates), pad() (a direction over the original coordinates placed on the wider width) and unit() (the direction of one added column).

Details

A filter writes \(\eta = F(s, \psi)\) from the static predictors \(s(u)\) of every equation and its own parameters. The kernels of the filter (jfp_joint_rows()) differentiate \(F\) with the static rows \(R = \partial s/\partial u\) held at their value, which is the whole derivative only where \(s\) is linear in \(u\). Where a block moves, the derivatives of \(s\) of order two and more are \(s''[a, b] = \partial R[a]\,b\) and so on (modelterms7::term_block_deriv() and its siblings), and the derivative of \(\eta\) along a set of indices is the sum over the partitions of the set into blocks, a block of one index entering \(F\) as a full direction and a block of \(j \ge 2\) indices as the static perturbation \(s^{(j)}\) along them. The kernels return every such term once the perturbations are placed as further unknowns: a column with the static rows \(x\) and no part in \(\psi\) is a direction along which \(F\) moves by \(x\) alone, so its entry in the kernels' result is the derivative of \(F\) with \(x\) in one argument. A free index that lies in a block of two or more indices is carried by one such column per value of the index.

The partitions written out are those of \(\{k, v\}\) and \(\{k, v, w\}\) for the rows, and of \(\{k, l\}\), \(\{k, l, v\}\) and \(\{k, l, v, w\}\) for the contraction, without the partition into singletons, which is the kernels' own result. In an equation that no filter drives \(F\) is the identity in that equation's static predictor, so the unknown's column enters there only through the contraction of the Jacobian.
